meaning: An extra amount on top of the basic State Pension, based on earnings and some credits before April 2016. It rises with prices, not with the triple lock.

The government's name for the rule it announced in September 2026 for April 2030. The pension would rise each year by inflation or 2.5%, whichever is higher, and by more if needed to keep pace with earnings over time. It is not in law.
A way of measuring income that takes off rent, mortgage interest, water charges and similar costs first.
The State Pension for people who reached State Pension age before 6 April 2016.
Amounts in the pounds of the year they were paid, with no adjustment for inflation.
Amounts adjusted for inflation so that different years can be compared. Also called real terms.
An official measure of how much consumer prices have changed. The triple lock uses the rise in this index over the 12 months to September.
Paying lower National Insurance in return for building up a workplace or personal pension instead of the Additional State Pension. It ended in April 2016.
A calculation of what would have happened under a different rule. It is not something that was paid.
Putting off a claim to the State Pension in return for a higher weekly amount later.

A rule that raises the pension by the higher of two measures. On this site it means the higher of prices and earnings. Some news reports use the term for the rule announced for April 2030, which is a different rule.
A rule that raises the pension in line with growth in average earnings.
The weekly amount for a person with the National Insurance record that the rules require. Many people receive less and some receive more.
A check of income, savings or both, used to decide who receives a benefit and how much.
The middle value. Half of the group is above it and half is below.
The account that receives most National Insurance contributions and pays the State Pension and some other benefits.
The State Pension for people who reached State Pension age on or after 6 April 2016.
A means-tested benefit that tops up the income of people over State Pension age. It has to be claimed.
A single pensioner, or a couple where at least one partner is over State Pension age. Used in official statistics on pensioner incomes.
An amount paid on top of the full new State Pension to a person whose starting amount in 2016 was higher than the full rate.
A tax year in which a person paid, or was credited with, enough National Insurance to count towards the State Pension.
A rule that follows earnings in the long run but rises with prices in years when earnings growth is lower, without a permanent gain.
The earliest age at which a person can claim the State Pension.
The share of people entitled to a benefit who claim it.
A government commitment to raise the basic and new State Pension each year by the highest of price inflation, earnings growth or 2.5%.
The yearly increase in the rate of a pension or benefit.
